Who we are

Precision positioning,
built in the open.

SparkPNT is the precision positioning company from the team behind SparkFun Electronics. Twenty-plus years of open-source hardware engineering, based in Colorado.

  • Open-source firmware. No black boxes, public roadmap, community-driven fixes.
  • A direct line to the engineers who design and build the hardware.
  • Designed for GIS field crews, not only for surveyors.

The lineup

One family. Three GNSS modules.

Every model comes with or without tilt compensation. The -T suffix means tilt is included. Same body, same firmware, either way.

FPL

Our pick

All-round GIS field work. Quad-band, four constellations, broadest correction support of the three. 48 h battery.

with tilt
without

FPX

Security-sensitive work. u-blox ZED-X20P with OSNMA signal authentication, so the receiver can tell a real Galileo signal from a spoofed one. 54 h battery.

with tilt
without

FPM

Hardest RF environments. Septentrio mosaic-X5 with AIM+ interference filtering. Logs RINEX natively for post-processing. 32 h battery.

with tilt
without

All models: IP67 cast-aluminum housing, LoRa base-to-rover radio, microSD logging, browser-based configuration.

Tilt compensation corrects for pole lean, so a valve box or a building corner can be measured without levelling the pole first.

Same RTK Everywhere firmware as the TX2. One firmware, every unit, updated together.

Built to be upgraded

Replace a module,
not a fleet.

The FP body is permanent. The GNSS module inside it swaps out with a Phillips screwdriver in about five minutes.

  • Your crew does the swap in-house. No RMA, no downtime.
  • Housing, antenna, battery, radio and IMU all stay in service.
  • One firmware across the line. An update improves every unit you own at once.
  • For a 10-14 unit fleet, a future upgrade is a line item, not a re-procurement.

Operating modes

One receiver, five jobs.

Rover

~700 mm
horizontal

No corrections beyond SBAS. Zero setup, fine for a quick locate.

Rover + RTK

8 / 15 mm
horizontal / vertical

RTCM corrections from a network, a base, or a radio. Fix in under 28 s.

Rover + PointPerfect

14 - 60 mm
horizontal

PPP-RTK, not RTK. Corrections modeled globally, sent over IP. No base at all. Fix up to 300 s.

Base Station

~100 m
radio range to rover

Survey-in takes 60 - 120 s, then it sends RTCM over the built-in 2.4 GHz radio.

Base + NTRIP Server

10 - 20 km
rover range, over internet

The same base publishes to up to four NTRIP casters. Rovers need internet, not radio.

You asked about base and rover. Any two units do it out of the box. The radio reaches about 100 m; past that, the base serves corrections over the internet.

Survey-in gives 8 mm relative to the base. The base's own absolute position can sit up to a meter off, so enter known coordinates when it must be absolute.

Configuration

Built for a fleet, built for utilities.

Profile configuration, on the device

Eight named profiles

Per unit. “Water crew,” “Sewer inverts,” “Base mode.” Standardize them across the fleet.

Correction priorities

Rank radio, Bluetooth, NTRIP and PointPerfect. Sources never blend or conflict.

Instrument heights

Antenna phase center plus pole height, so every point references the pole tip.

Fleet firmware

Over-the-air updates. One firmware across the TX2 and the FP line, moved together.

docs.sparkpnt.com/TX2/correction_services ↗
Vertical accuracy for utilities

Vertical is where utility work gets hard.

Gravity mains and inverts in flat terrain. A few centimeters can change which way the line appears to fall.

Realistic expectation

Vertical error typically runs 1.5 to 2 times the horizontal error.

Tilt compensation

-T units correct pole lean at valve boxes, fence lines and building corners. No re-leveling.
